issues.legal_issue: A court's power to excuse a tenant's late rent deposit is limited by the rent-control scheme governing the eviction proceeding.
material_facts: In an eviction suit, the court determined provisional rent and directed the tenant to deposit arrears and continuing rent within specified periods.
The tenant did not deposit the rent within the time allowed and later sought condonation of the delay.
The governing scheme permitted only a limited extension and directed the court to strike out the defence if the tenant failed to deposit rent within the specified time.
The High Court allowed the tenant's challenge, but the Supreme Court set aside that judgment.
issues.conclusion: The court had no power to extend the deposit period beyond the statutory limit or to condone the tenant's default; the late deposit could not be excused.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 13(4) and 13(5) of the Rajasthan Premises (Control of Rent & Eviction) Act, 1950, the court may extend the deposit period only within the specified limits, and failure to deposit within the prescribed or extended period requires the defence against eviction to be struck out. The word “shall,” read with the scheme and its stated consequence, is mandatory. M/s B.P. Khemka Pvt. Ltd. v. Birendra Kumar Bhowmick does not govern because the West Bengal Act considered there expressly conferred a power to extend time without the same restriction. The Court also relied on the principle that clear statutory language cannot be rewritten to avoid harsh consequences, as reflected in Union of India v. Filip Tiago De Gama of Vedem Vasco De Gama, Bhavnagar University v. Palitana Sugar Mill Pvt. Ltd., and M/s Unique Butyle Tube Industries Pvt. Ltd. v. U.P. Financial Corporation.

predicates.rent_control_eviction_suit: A landlord brought a suit seeking eviction of a tenant under a rent-control scheme.
predicates.tenant_missed_rent_deposit_deadline: The tenant failed to deposit rent by the deadline set by the court or within an extension granted under the governing scheme.
predicates.governing_scheme_allows_only_limited_ext: The governing scheme permits only a bounded extension for depositing rent and does not authorize the court to excuse a default beyond that limit.

issues.definition: When a tenant misses the rent-deposit deadline in a rent-control eviction suit and the governing scheme permits only a limited extension, the court cannot excuse the late deposit.

issues.legal_issue: The general power to extend limitation does not apply to a tenant's late compliance with a court-ordered rent deposit requirement.
material_facts: In an eviction suit, the court ordered the tenant to deposit provisional rent and continuing rent within specified periods.
The tenant defaulted on that deposit requirement and later applied to have the delay condoned.
The deposit was compliance with a court order, not an appeal or an application that had to be admitted after the prescribed period.
The governing scheme specified consequences for failing to make the deposit and did not confer power to condone that default.
issues.conclusion: Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1963 does not apply to a tenant's default in depositing rent under the court's order.
issues.legal_principle: Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1963 permits an appeal or application to be admitted after the prescribed period on sufficient cause; it does not extend time for a deposit that is not itself an appeal or application. Read with Section 3 of that Act, it does not provide a basis to condone failure to comply with a court order where the governing scheme specifies the consequences of default and confers no such power. The Court relied on Hukumdev Narain Yadav v. Lalit Narain Mishra, Commissioner of Sales Tax v. Parson Tools and Plants, and Prem Raj v. Ram Charan. Mukri Gopalan v. Cheppilat Puthanpurayil Aboobacker and Shantilal M. Bhayani v. Shanti Bai were distinguishable because they concerned limitation for appeals.

predicates.rent_control_eviction_suit: A landlord brought a suit seeking eviction of a tenant under a rent-control scheme.
predicates.rent_deposit_is_compliance_with_court_or: The tenant was required to deposit rent to comply with an order made by the court in the eviction proceeding.
predicates.no_application_is_required_for_deposit: The tenant's rent deposit was not an appeal or application that had to be filed or admitted within a prescribed period.

issues.definition: If a tenant's rent deposit is compliance with a court order and no application is required to make the deposit in a rent-control eviction suit, Section 5 does not apply to the late deposit.
